issues.evidence: Tibetan དེ་སྙེད་བསྐལ་པར ("for that many eons") is a correlative of ཇི་སྙེད་པ; 爾等 means "you (pl.)" in Chinese and does not render the demonstrative "that many".

Tibetan ཐབ་སྐྱོན་ལྡན་སེམས (Skt khila-doṣa); bo-mipham 5-33 glosses it as a mind with the fault 'like a hearth' (ཐ་བ་ལྟ་བུ་སྐྱོན) from a continuum unfit, in which seeds of virtue do not grow, i.e. barrenness, not generic 'bad' quality.

issues.span: 「佛依安忍波羅蜜多證得菩提。」
issues.evidence: In the Tibetan the first line is the premise of the thought, not a separate quotation: bo-mipham 5-34 and bo-khenrab 5-34 read 'if Buddhas touch awakening by patience, then this angry mind of mine is not good (སེམས་འདི་བཟང་བ་མིན་སྙམ)'. Setting line 1 in its own quotation marks detaches it from the thought and leaves the following clause grammatically orphaned.
issues.fix: 佛依安忍波羅蜜多證得菩提，（既然如此）

issues.span: 彼為得佛功德而於此修學
issues.evidence: Tibetan སངས་རྒྱས་ཅོས་མཉེས་བྱ་ཕྱིར means 'in order to please' (མཉེས་བྱ; Skt ārādhiteṣu). bo-rangjung 5-36 reads སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་ཀྱིས་མཉེས་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར; bo-mipham 5-36 gives 'attain' as one reading but also notes the 'please' reading. The translation renders only 'attain' and drops མཉེས.
issues.fix: 彼為以佛功德令（諸佛）歡喜而於此修學

issues.evidence: Following 有情 immediately, 彼等 reads as the sentient beings who seek virtue. bo-mipham 5-42 shows དེ་དག refers to the irreversible bodhisattvas who rejoice (མི་ལྡོག་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་དག ... རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཐོབ་པར་གྱུར་ནས), who also are the unstated subject of ཡི་རང་གྱུར.
issues.fix: 是故彼等（隨喜之）菩薩獲得勝者功德後

issues.span: 四魔難以勝伏亦不能動搖
issues.evidence: Tibetan བདུད་བཞིས་ཐུབ་པར་དཀའ་ཞིང་བསྐྱོད་པར་མི་ནུས: the four Māras are the agent (instrumental བཞིས), the bodhisattva is the one hard to overcome and impossible to shake (bo-mipham 5-51: བདུད་བཞིས་ཐུབ་པར་དཀའ་ཞིང་ལམ་ལས་བསྐྱོད་པར་མི་ནུས). In the Chinese the four Māras stand as grammatical subject of 難以勝伏, so it reads that the Māras are hard to subdue, reversing the relation.
issues.fix: 彼為四魔所難以勝伏，亦不能為四魔所動搖
